raw_response:
Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral pulmonary nodules and prominent hilar lymphadenopathy, which are classic radiographic features of sarcoidosis (often referred to as the "sarcoid galaxy sign" when small nodules cluster around a larger one on CT, though the CXR findings of bilateral nodules and adenopathy strongly support this diagnosis over the other options).
